fixtures.source: New synthetic temporary project directories only; no user Git repository or external resources accessed.

caseDefinition.steps: Legal filenames with quotes, semicolon, backticks, $() and newline; system opener stub records arguments.
caseDefinition.expected: Paths remain data arguments without string-shell execution; unsupported protocols are rejected; filename content is never executed.

tests: M12: preserves quotes, semicolons, backticks, substitution syntax and newline as exact OS opener arguments
M12: rejects unsupported protocols and forged external application choices before OS dispatch
chain: Unmodified production native broker including application discovery and identity checks

assertions: Each original filename remains exactly one Foundation file-reference URL path at the actual NSWorkspace call boundary.
All actual broker spawns use a fixed executable, empty argv and no shell option.
File bytes, size, mtimeNs and inode unchanged after all opener requests.
Unissued app identifiers and forged executable path rejected before NSWorkspace dispatch.
I.filenameExecutionEvidence: Metacharacter strings are preserved literally in actual OS method parameters; production path uses NSWorkspace typed URLs rather than a shell command. The test process records its actual child spawn shape. The only substituted code is the final OS call, so no external application or filename command runs. The synthetic printf spellings are inert filenames, not commands sent to a shell.

codeAudit.finding: Fixed executable spawn with [] arguments and no shell.
NSWorkspace receives a single validated file-reference NSURL and independently checked application NSURL, without string command construction.

limits: Original case explicitly requires I and permits an opener stub. This record makes no P/A GUI or external TextEdit execution claim.
macOS arm64 only; no Windows/Linux extrapolation.
NSWorkspace uses typed URL arguments rather than a CLI argv. The recorded typed arguments are the platform equivalent of the case opener argv requirement.
